header.one_line: Nepal from the border at Sunauli up the Siddhartha Highway to Pokhara, then the Kali Gandaki valley to Jomsom and Muktinath

rules.title: Nepal: customs pass for an Indian-registered vehicle
rules.detail: Issued by Nepal Customs at the border for a stated number of days, two-wheelers included. The Indian embassy gives the charge as 100 to 500 Nepalese rupees a day.
rules.set_by: Department of Customs, Government of Nepal

source.title: Embassy of India, Kathmandu: entry of Indian registered vehicles in Nepal

rules.title: Nepal: 30 days a year for an Indian vehicle
rules.detail: An Indian-registered vehicle may stay 30 days in total in a calendar year. An extension must be sought at a Nepal Customs office before the pass expires.
rules.set_by: Department of Customs, Government of Nepal

source.title: Embassy of India, Kathmandu: entry of Indian registered vehicles in Nepal

rules.title: Nepal: free day pass only to the nearest market
rules.detail: A day pass lets a vehicle visit the nearest town without customs charge. It must return to India the same day and hand the pass back.
rules.set_by: Department of Customs, Government of Nepal

source.title: Embassy of India, Kathmandu: entry of Indian registered vehicles in Nepal

rules.title: Nepal: vehicle without a valid pass is seized
rules.detail: A vehicle found without a pass, or with an expired one, is treated as smuggled, confiscated and later auctioned by Nepal Customs.
rules.set_by: Department of Customs, Government of Nepal

source.title: Embassy of India, Kathmandu: entry of Indian registered vehicles in Nepal

rules.title: Nepal: passport or original voter card
rules.detail: For air travel the embassy accepts only a passport or an original voter identity card; Aadhaar and driving licence are refused. The page does not cover land crossings.
rules.set_by: Government of Nepal, as stated by the Embassy of India, Kathmandu

source.title: Embassy of India, Kathmandu: valid travel documents

rules.title: Annapurna Conservation Area: entry permit
rules.detail: Costs 1,000 Nepalese rupees for citizens of South Asian countries and 3,000 for other foreigners. Single entry; bought online or at a counter; shown at check posts.
rules.set_by: National Trust for Nature Conservation, Nepal

source.title: National Trust for Nature Conservation: online entry permit

rules.title: Upper Mustang: restricted area permit, 50 dollars a day
rules.detail: Covers Lomanthang and Lo-Ghekar Damodarkunda, plus ward 3 and Satang village of Baragung Muktichhetra. Issued by the immigration department in Kathmandu. Needed only beyond this route.
rules.applies_to: Foreign visitors going north of this route
rules.set_by: Department of Immigration, Government of Nepal

source.title: Nepal Tourism Board: trekking permit

history.change: Wikipedia still records the older fee of 500 dollars for ten days, then 50 dollars a day; the date of the change was not found.

season.note: No seasonal closure of the road to Jomsom and Muktinath was found; the monsoon from June to September is the difficult season.

hazards.title: Rockfall between Butwal and Palpa
hazards.detail: Wikipedia describes this section of the Siddhartha Highway as rocky, with frequent rockfall that sometimes causes fatal accidents.

source.title: Siddhartha Highway

hazards.title: Monsoon rain south of the Himalaya
hazards.detail: The tourism board says four-fifths of Nepal's rain falls from June to September. Mustang itself lies in a rain shadow and stays dry.

source.title: Nepal Tourism Board: climate

hazards.title: Strong daily wind in the Kali Gandaki valley
hazards.detail: Wind blowing up the valley is strong enough to stop flights from Jomsom after about 11 in the morning.

source.title: Jomsom

hazards.title: Road works on the Kali Gandaki corridor
hazards.detail: Wikipedia lists the highway through Beni and Kagbeni as under construction since December 2018, with its completion status unclear.

source.title: Kaligandaki Corridor

gaps: Web search budget ran out before this route; all facts come from pages opened directly.
The exact daily customs charge for a motorcycle was not found; the embassy page gives only a range for all vehicles.
Nepal's Department of Customs site was not opened; the vehicle rules are as stated by the Embassy of India.
Documents asked for at the border for the vehicle (registration, licence, insurance) are not listed on the embassy page.
Documents for Indian citizens crossing by land are not stated on the embassy page, which covers air travel.
Whether Muktinath and Kagbeni fall outside the restricted wards was not confirmed from an official map; the rule records the wards as listed.
Whether Indian citizens need the Upper Mustang permit, and at what fee, was not found.
No source found on any local vehicle fee or check post rule for motorcycles in Mustang.
No dated source found for landslides or closures on the Beni to Jomsom road.
The highway number beyond Pokhara (NH48, Kali Gandaki corridor) comes from a separate Wikipedia article.
Usual number of days not sourced.
The tourism board's travel updates page was too large to open; the immigration department's site returned a certificate error.
